subject: Re: Redwood Private / VPC pricing — follow-up & licensing questions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Redwood Private / VPC pricing — post-demo recap

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can align on pricing and next steps: 

1) Use case & scale
- Primary: customer-facing chat and some batch summarization for regulatory reports.
- Expected peak: ~250 req/sec, average prompt+response ~800 tokens, with heavy tail to 2k tokens.

2) Key asks from you
- Licensing model for Private/VPC (per-environment vs per-node vs per-seat)
- Support tier options and response SLAs
- Environment counts (prod/staging/dev) and approx concurrency per env
- Target unit economics — you mentioned target $/1M tokens on the call

3) What we can offer (high level) — we'll follow up with a detailed deck and pricing sheet attached: Redwood_Private_Pricing_v2.pdf
- Licensing: perpetual-like termed license + annual platform fee OR subscription per-environment. For commitments we can do blended $/1M token pricing plus per-environment overhead.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours), Premium (24/7 with 1-hour P1), Enterprise (dedicated TAM + quarterly reviews).
- Options to include dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) and on-prem package for air-gapped deployments.

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm environment counts (prod/staging/dev), expected steady-state concurrent sessions by env, and target $/1M tokens (ballpark)
- Ben/Markus: share pricing deck + proposed mutual action plan (attached) and a draft licensing summary.

Thanks — aiming to have a first draft proposal by Wed EOD PT.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood Private / VPC pricing — post-demo recap

Thanks Ben — quick answers below, appreciate the fast follow-up.

Environments:
- Prod: 1 (global)
- Staging: 1
- Dev: ~4 (shared)

Concurrency / volumes (estimates):
- Steady-state: ~120 concurrent requests across prod at peak hours
- Average tokens per request: 700 tokens
- Monthly throughput: targeting ~1.5 billion tokens/month initially, scaling to 4B over 12 months as we roll out new features.

Budget / unit economics:
- Target ASA (approx): we have internal target of ~$60–$80 per 1M tokens for hosted, but for Private/VPC we can go higher because of network/infra. Team is comfortable with $200–$350 per 1M tokens depending on support/SLA and whether we commit to a 12–24 month term.

Licensing preferences:
- Prefer per-environment subscription for clarity, but open to a mixed model if committed throughput discounts are significant.

Next: procurement will want a SKUized quote (single-line items: environments, support tier, committed tokens/month).

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure, FintechCo

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood Private / VPC pricing — post-demo recap

Appreciate the details, Alex — that's super helpful. A few clarifying questions and a preliminary approach based on your ranges: 

Clarifying Qs:
- The 1.5B/month initial: is that total tokens across prompts+responses? (Assuming yes, we'll run unit economics on 1.5B.)
- For dev: are the ~4 dev environments low-capacity (shared, best-effort) or do you expect reserved capacity per dev environment?

Preliminary pricing approach (ballpark, subject to legal/finance review):
- Licensing model options:
  a) Per-environment subscription: $Xk/month per prod/staging (prod higher), $Yk/month for dev shared. Includes control-plane and standard updates.
  b) Committed throughput discount: reserve >=1B tokens/month => blended unit price in range $150–$260 per 1M tokens depending on support tier and quantization/optimizations.
  c) On-prem/air-gapped add-on: one-time onboarding & integration fee + per-node runtime license.

- Support tiers impact: Standard (no premium on token price), Premium (+~30% on unit price), Enterprise (+~55% and TAM hours).

I'll attach a draft SKU table (Mutual_Action_Plan_FintechCo.xlsx) and the pricing PDF. Markus, can you weigh in on the per-node runtime license / typical node counts we would recommend for their traffic profile?

Next steps: I'll put together two formal options: (1) subscription-per-environment + low committed throughput, (2) committed throughput + lower $/1M + per-environment fees. Will aim to get to Alex & procurement by EOD today.

Ben
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood Private / VPC pricing — node sizing + ops notes

Alex / team — quick technical note to help with licensing/price callouts: 

- Based on ~120 concurrent requests at 700 tokens avg (1.5B/mo), we typically recommend a small dedicated cluster: 6 GPU nodes (A100/80GB equiv) for prod with autoscaling headroom. Staging can be 1 node, dev shared as burstable on smaller machines.
- For licensing: per-node runtime license makes sense if you want full on-prem. If you prefer per-environment subscription, the per-node model lets you scale node count independently (useful for bursty workloads).
- Ops + onboarding: estimate 4–6 weeks for VPC setup, customer-managed KMS, and validation tests for SOC2 requirements.

If Alex confirms dev environments are best-effort (no reserved nodes), our commercial proposal will reflect lower dev fees.

-Markus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex / Procurement — attaching the formal proposal as discussed. High-level summary / ask from FintechCo to confirm so we can finalize commercial SKUs: 

1) Environments: Prod=1 (reserved), Staging=1 (reserved), Dev=4 (shared, best-effort) — please confirm.
2) Committed throughput: confirm whether you want to commit to 1.5B tokens/mo for 12 months (preferred) or start with month-to-month. Committed term gets you to the ~$150–$200/1M target in the draft.
3) Support tier: let us know whether Standard / Premium / Enterprise. Procurement usually signs off faster on Standard + 9x5 with optional Premium add-on.

Attached: Redwood_Private_Pricing_v2.pdf, Mutual_Action_Plan_FintechCo.xlsx

If these align I’ll push a SKUized quote to procurement and loop in legal for a redlineable contract (we can do a 60–90 day signature timeline).

Best,
Ben
